subTopic: Social justice, true religion and divine love - Hosea 4:12-13
question: Hosea accused Israel of harlotry because
options: the women ran after other husbands
explanation: Hosea 1:2 says the land commits harlotry by forsaking the LORD; 4:12 says 'a spirit of harlotry has led them astray, and they have left their God to play the harlot.' Harlotry symbolizes idolatry.
proTip: In Hosea, harlotry is spiritual unfaithfulness - worshipping other gods.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: Who among the following was consecrated and appointed prophet before he was born?
explanation: Jeremiah 1:5: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.'
proTip: Jeremiah's call: known, consecrated and appointed before birth.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: 'Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you.' The statement above was made during the call of
explanation: Ezekiel 2:1: 'And he said to me, "Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you."' God addressed Ezekiel as 'son of man' throughout the book.
proTip: 'Son of man' is God's usual address to Ezekiel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Baptism and Temptation of Jesus - Matthew 4:8-10
question: Satan promised to give Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if He would
options: turn stones to loaves of bread
throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple
explanation: Matthew 4:8-9: the devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and said, 'All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me.'
proTip: The third temptation in Matthew: worship of Satan for world power.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The would-be disciple who wanted to go and bury his father before following Jesus was told that he
options: was not fit for the kingdom of God
should go and proclaim the kingdom of God
should go and build a house first
explanation: Luke 9:60: 'Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but as for you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.'
proTip: Following Jesus and proclaiming the kingdom comes first.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Discipleship - the call of the first disciples (Matthew 4:18-20)
question: According to Matthew, the first two disciples to be called by Jesus were
explanation: Matthew 4:18-20: Simon called Peter and Andrew, his brother, were called first; James and John were called next (4:21-22).
proTip: Matthew's order: Peter and Andrew first, then James and John.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus had compassion for the five thousand people fed by Him because they were
options: hungry but had no time to eat
strangers from the country and villages far away
poor and had no money to buy food
explanation: Mark 6:34: 'he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.' (Matthew 14:14 says He healed their sick.)
proTip: Mark 6:34: compassion because they were like sheep without a shepherd.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What was Jesus' response when the message of Lazarus' illness reached Him?
options: He asked Mary and Martha to take care of him
He said that the Son of God may be glorified by it
He hurried to Bethany to see him
He instructed that he should be brought to Him
explanation: John 11:4: 'This illness is not unto death; it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified by means of it.' He stayed two more days where He was (11:6).
proTip: Jesus delayed, saying the illness was for the glory of God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: At the country of the Gerasenes, Jesus
options: raised Jairus' daughter from the dead
raised the widow's son from the dead
healed the man who had demons
explanation: Mark 5:1-20 and Luke 8:26-39 record Jesus healing the man possessed by a legion of demons in the country of the Gerasenes; the demons entered the swine.
proTip: Gerasenes = the man with a legion of demons.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Parables - the Wheat and the Tares (Matthew 13:24-30)
question: The parable of the wheat and the tares illustrates that
options: the kingdom of God is already established on earth
both good and evil live in the world
it is impossible to overcome enemies
the wheat cannot grow where there are weeds
explanation: The householder said, 'Let both grow together until the harvest' (Matthew 13:30). Good and evil coexist until the final judgment.
proTip: Wheat and tares: good and evil coexist until the harvest.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus' teaching on swearing is that Christians should
explanation: Matthew 5:34, 37: 'Do not swear at all... Let what you say be simply "Yes" or "No".'
proTip: Jesus: let your 'Yes' be yes and your 'No' be no.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Sermon on the Mount - the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:8)
question: What blessing has Jesus promised the pure in heart?
options: The earth shall be theirs only
explanation: Matthew 5:8: 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.' Mercy is for the merciful (5:7), comfort for those who mourn (5:4).
proTip: Match each beatitude with its blessing.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'The harvest is plentiful, but the labourers are few...' Jesus made the statement above during the
explanation: Luke 10:1-2 records Jesus appointing 'seventy others' and telling them 'The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few.' Matthew 9:37-38 has the same saying before the mission of the twelve, so check against your key.
proTip: The harvest saying is in Luke 10:2 (seventy) and Matthew 9:37 (before the twelve).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing - Matthew 21:9
question: '...Hosanna to the Son of David!...' The statement above indicates Jesus'
explanation: 'Son of David' is a messianic title meaning the promised king from David's line. The crowd welcomed Jesus as the Messiah-King (Matthew 21:9).
proTip: 'Son of David' = Messiah and King.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing - Luke 19:28-40
question: With regard to the triumphal entry, which of the following descriptions is peculiar to Luke?
options: The disciples were sent to bring the animal
People spread their garments on the road
The disciples set Jesus on the animal
explanation: Luke 19:35 says the disciples 'set Jesus on' the colt. In Matthew 21:7 and Mark 11:7, Jesus sat on it. Hosanna (Matthew, Mark), sending for the animal and spreading garments appear in more than one gospel.
proTip: Luke 19:35: the disciples set Jesus on the colt.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Matthew 26:57
question: According to Matthew, when Christ was arrested, He was led to
explanation: Matthew 26:57: 'Those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.' (John 18:13 mentions Annas first.)
proTip: Matthew: Jesus was led to Caiaphas; John: first to Annas.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Matthew 26:63-66
question: The conviction of Jesus by the high priest and the elders was on the ground that He
options: said He would destroy the temple
explanation: After Jesus affirmed He was the Christ, the Son of God, the high priest tore his robes and said, 'He has uttered blasphemy' (Matthew 26:65); they judged Him deserving death.
proTip: The Sanhedrin's verdict: blasphemy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In the account of John about the resurrection, Mary was first asked why she was weeping by
explanation: John 20:12-13: Mary saw two angels in white at the tomb who asked, 'Woman, why are you weeping?' Then Jesus asked her the same (20:15).
proTip: In John 20, the angels ask first, then Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Acts 1:23-26
question: 'Lord, who knowest the hearts of all men, show which one of these two thou hast chosen to take the place from which Judas turned aside...' Who were the two men referred to in the statement above?
explanation: Acts 1:23: they put forward Joseph called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias. Since 'Justus' is Joseph's surname, option A names the two candidates by distinct names. (Options B, C and D each name only Joseph/Barsabbas/Justus, the same man; check against your key.)
proTip: Candidates for Judas' place: Joseph Barsabbas (Justus) and Matthias.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Acts 6:3
question: The criteria for the choice of the seven deacons were
options: good repute and being full of the Spirit
explanation: Acts 6:3: 'pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom.' Good repute and being full of the Spirit is the closest option.
proTip: Deacon qualifications: good repute, full of the Spirit (and wisdom).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: At Pentecost, Peter explained that God had promised to pour out His Spirit on all
explanation: Acts 2:17 (quoting Joel 2:28): 'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh.'
proTip: Acts 2:17: 'all flesh' - the promise is universal.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:28-29)
question: The resolution of the Jerusalem council was that the Gentiles should abstain from food offered to idols,
options: unchastity, lying and what is strangled
blood, what is strangled and strong drinks
what is strangled, blood and unchastity
explanation: Acts 15:29: 'that you abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity.'
proTip: The four requirements: idols, blood, strangled animals, unchastity.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders... to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas'; who were the men chosen?
explanation: Acts 15:22: 'Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren.' Judas Barsabbas and Silas carried the Council's letter to Antioch.
proTip: Judas Barsabbas and Silas delivered the Council's letter.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Peter and John were arrested and imprisoned because they
options: healed a man lame from birth
condemned the Pharisees and the Sadducees
were preaching the gospel of Jesus
explanation: Acts 4:1-3: the priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees arrested them because they were 'teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.' The healing (Acts 3) led to the occasion, but preaching was the stated ground.
proTip: The charge was preaching the resurrection in Jesus' name.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Romans, all who have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God will be justified by
options: the worship of God through Christ
explanation: Romans 3:23-24: 'all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, they are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus.'
proTip: Justified by grace as a gift.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Paul, what bear witness to the righteousness of God are
explanation: Romans 3:21: 'the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from law, although the law and the prophets bear witness to it.'
proTip: The law and the prophets bear witness to God's righteousness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: The consequence of setting one's mind on the things of the flesh is
explanation: Romans 8:6: 'To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.'
proTip: Flesh = death; Spirit = life and peace.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul admonished the Romans to live a new life in Christ by yielding themselves to God as men who
options: have been brought from death to life
will receive judgment in the last days
will meet Christ in God's kingdom
have suffered for the sake of the gospel
explanation: Romans 6:13: 'yield yourselves to God as men who have been brought from death to life.'
proTip: Believers yield to God as those raised from death to life.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: 'But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian...' Custodian here means the
explanation: Galatians 3:24-25: 'the law was our custodian until Christ came... But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian.'
proTip: The custodian is the law.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul, writing to the Philippians, said that God highly exalted Christ and bestowed on Him the name which is above every name because He was
explanation: Philippians 2:8-9: 'he humbled himself and became obedient unto death... Therefore God has highly exalted him.'
proTip: The 'therefore' of Philippians 2:9 gives the reason: humility and obedience.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Paul, Christians should forgive one another so that
options: Satan may not gain advantage over them
they may not perish in sin
explanation: 2 Corinthians 2:10-11: 'Any one whom you forgive, I also forgive... so that we may not be outwitted by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his designs.'
proTip: Unforgiveness gives Satan an advantage.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Spiritual gifts, according to Paul, should be used for the
options: upliftment of individuals in the church
explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:12 says to strive to excel in gifts 'for building up the church', and verse 26 repeats that all things be done for edification.
proTip: Gifts are for building up the church.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul considered the Philippians' gifts to him as
options: an exhibition of Christian maturity and generosity
a fragrant offering and a sacrifice acceptable to God
explanation: Philippians 4:18: 'I have received full payment... the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God.'
proTip: Giving to God's work is a fragrant offering to God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: 'For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad.' Christians, therefore, must do what is good and they would
options: be left alone to preach the Gospel
explanation: Romans 13:3: 'Would you have no fear of him who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval.'
proTip: Do good and you will have the authorities' approval.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: 'Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from any brother who is living in idleness...' The statement above was made to teach
explanation: Paul told the idlers to work quietly and earn their own living (2 Thessalonians 3:10-12), teaching the dignity of labour.
proTip: 2 Thessalonians 3: work and earn your own bread.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: The second coming of Jesus Christ, according to Paul, will be preceded by the coming of
explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:3: 'that day will not come, unless the rebellion comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed.'
proTip: The man of lawlessness must be revealed before the Day of the Lord.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: 'Is it not the rich who oppress you, is it not they who drag you into court?' James asked this question in his teaching on
explanation: James 2:6 appears in the passage condemning favouritism to the rich in the assembly (2:1-9).
proTip: James 2: do not favour the rich over the poor.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: The wisdom of God is necessary for salvation, hence James teaches that Christians should
options: ask for it when they can
endure all trials to get it
ask in faith to get it
explanation: James 1:5-6: 'If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God... But let him ask in faith, with no doubting.'
proTip: Ask God for wisdom in faith, without doubting.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 4:8
question: The importance of love in the teaching of Peter is that it
options: brings together all believers in the community
explanation: 1 Peter 4:8: 'Above all hold unfailing your love for one another, since love covers a multitude of sins.'
proTip: 1 Peter 4:8: love covers a multitude of sins.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 5:1-4
question: According to Peter, when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, Christians will
options: cast all their anxieties on Him
obtain the unfading crown of glory
explanation: 1 Peter 5:4: 'when the chief Shepherd is manifested you will obtain the unfading crown of glory.'
proTip: The faithful receive 'the unfading crown of glory'.
